items.title: Frank Foster — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He didn’t sound like Tommy Flanagan or Hank Jones or John Hicks or whoever you might like to think of in a modern vein.

ctx.x: Didn’t allow you to do that.

Basie didn’t play like McCoy Tyner. When he’d comp behind solos, he didn’t sound like Tommy Flanagan or Hank Jones or John Hicks or whoever you might like to think of in a modern vein. When he played it was a very harmonically limited style as far as the bebop idiom was concerned. He’s still back in 1937 with his comping and his chord structures.
So he’s not laying out, just to regurgitate what you’re saying. He’s not putting it under you to play off of, and his conception isn’t going in that direction anyway.
